newsitem.title: USA: Great Western files counterclaim against Ahmanson.
newsitem.headline: Great Western files counterclaim against Ahmanson.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp. filed a counterclaim Wednesday against H.F. Ahmanson and Co. related to the thrift's $6.2 billion hostile bid for Great Western.

In a statement, Great Western said the proposed by-law amendment under which Ahmanson is soliciting consents is "illegal" and "unenforceable" and is "an improper intrusion into the statutory powers of the board of directors."
Ahmanson, based in Irwindale, Calif., offered to buy rival Great Western in a stock transaction that would create a powerful thrift in the quickly-consolidating California market.

So far, Great Western has not replied to Ahmanson's offer, fuelling speculation the thrift is trying to forge a more favourable deal with another institution such as Norwest Corp., or Washington Mutual Savings Bank.

In its counterclaim, Great Western is seeking to block Ahmanson's attempt to establish a ceiling for any "lock-up" agreeement the thrift might set with another bidder. In corporate takeovers, a lock up agreement is a fee that two merging companies set to discourage either company from walking away.

Ahmanson is seeking to set the ceiling at $100 million but Great Western would prefer it to be higher so other bidders would not be turned off by a low payout in the event Ahmanson came forward with a higher offer.
Great Western also is seeking to block Ahmanson's attempts to eliminate Great Western's poison pill, a move that would make it more expensive for Ahmanson to aquire the thrift.
On Tuesday, Great Western postponed its annual meeting from its previously-scheduled date of April 22. A new date has not been set.
Great Western also created an employee severance programme that could raise the cost of a takeover from Ahmanson.
Great Western closed at $46.50 a share, down 37.5 cents, and Ahmanson closed at $42 a share, up 50 cents, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
